claims.text: ASP.NET Core middleware registered with app.Use... calls runs in the exact order those calls appear in Program.cs, and the response passes back through them in reverse order, so the first one registered is usually the last to finish.

A middleware can run code before it calls the next delegate and after that call returns. ASP.NET Core constructs a middleware class once, passing next (a RequestDelegate) to its constructor, then per request calls its method found by the name InvokeAsync with that request's HttpContext.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs, Middleware: write custom middleware

claims.text: A middleware short-circuits the pipeline by not calling the next delegate, usually after writing a response itself; nothing registered after it then runs, so if RequestLoggingMiddleware ran after UseAuthorization instead of before, it would not log a request UseAuthorization rejected.

UseAuthentication doesn't reject a request lacking credentials; it calls next with no caller identified. UseAuthorization must come after it and before endpoint execution; for an [Authorize] endpoint it stops a request not permitted: 401 (challenge) if no caller identified, 403 (forbid) if known.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs, Authentication overview (challenge, forbid); Middleware order ('must appear in the order shown'); Routing fundamentals

claims.text: RequestLoggingMiddleware calls next(context), and once next returns (even early, after a short-circuit) logs method, path, status code and elapsed time via logger.LogInformation: one log entry in the API's output (the message line under an 'info:' header line), shown by docker compose logs api.

Sending POST /api/v1/orders with no Authorization header to the stage-1 lab (scripts/up.sh from the repo's top folder; needs Docker and the Flutter SDK) returns 401; curl -i prints the status line and headers; docker compose logs api shows a RequestLoggingMiddleware line reporting 401.

claims.text: ASP.NET Core adds middleware of its own: routing matches a request to an endpoint before user-registered middleware runs; endpoint execution runs what app.MapControllers() registered only after every middleware ran without short-circuiting. The endpoint is terminal: it calls nothing further.
